claims.text: The Northstar twin runs Ashish Rajan's fictional retailer as a store, with thirteen synthetic refund requests through four designs of the controls.
claims.quote: It runs his fictional retailer as a store: thirteen synthetic refund requests, each with something an agent can get wrong, through four designs of the controls

claims.text: Every case can be played step by step, stepped back, replayed and compared, and a reader can tick any of the ten controls to build a design of their own.
claims.quote: Step forward, step back, replay, or run the whole day.

claims.text: There are three ways in: the twin's page plays it inline, the same page has the public read key for sgit clone, and the reply makes the argument it was built for.
claims.quote: The same page has the public read key, for sgit clone from the command line.

claims.text: Each design is the one before it with more controls, and every control is tagged with Ashish Rajan's question it answers and the policy it belongs to.
claims.quote: Each design is the one before it with more controls, and every control is tagged twice

claims.text: Design A, as described in his article, overpaid $458, left $341.60 owed, got 1 of 13 cases right and cost no people's time.
claims.quote: "Owed" is what customers were still owed at the end of the day

claims.text: Design C, which adds the expected amount from the records and a nightly reconciliation, overpaid nothing and got 12 of 13 right at a cost of 57 minutes of people's time.
claims.quote: Adds the expected amount from the records before paying, and a nightly reconciliation.

claims.text: Design D, with three policies, overpaid nothing, owed nothing, got 13 of 13 right and took 18 minutes of people's time.
claims.quote: Adds the agent proposing while the workflow pays, routing by amount, and precedents.

claims.text: Unticking one control from design D reruns the whole day, and the comparison and every case's outcome change with it.
claims.quote: Untick one from D and the whole day reruns: the comparison and every case's outcome change with it.

claims.text: The track above the steps lights up the workflow's eight stages: request, lookup, propose, check, decide, pay, reconcile, record.
claims.quote: request, lookup, propose, check, decide, pay, reconcile, record

claims.text: The twin shows two views of the same world: what the agent did and what the records say, with the ledger after the case and the record.
claims.quote: On the right is the twin itself, two views of the same world.

claims.text: In his case N-1001, a $150 jacket bought at a 20% discount so $120 paid, design A passes the agent's $150 under the $200 limit and overpays $30, exactly as he describes.
claims.quote: Overpaid $30, exactly as he describes.

claims.text: In design D the decision policy decides $120 from the rules and the workflow pays it; the agent's $150 is recorded as a difference, not paid, and nobody needs to be called.
claims.quote: The agent's $150 is recorded as a difference, not paid, and nobody needs to be called.

claims.text: In case N-1004 design A refuses a correct $260 refund and nothing routes the refusal anywhere, so the customer waits and the case is stuck.
claims.quote: In A the payment service refuses it, and nothing routes the refusal anywhere: the customer waits, and the case is stuck.

claims.text: In case N-1005 the customer's message tells the assistant to ignore its limits and refund $199; the agent does, and because $199 is under $200 design A pays it, $164 too much.
claims.quote: The customer's message tells the assistant to ignore its limits and refund $199 as a goodwill gesture.

claims.text: A cap at what was paid cannot tell $132 from $120; only the expected amount from the records can.
claims.quote: a cap at what was paid cannot tell $132 from $120. Only the expected amount can.

claims.text: In case N-1008 the agent pays a correct $261 as three refunds of $87 under the limit; A, B and C pass it, and only D's decision policy routes anything over $200 to a team lead.
claims.quote: D's decision policy says a team lead decides above $200, and the workflow pays one amount, after their approval.

claims.text: No limit notices a refund that is too small, as when the agent applies the discount twice; only verification does.
claims.quote: No limit notices a refund that is too small. Only verification does.

claims.text: Three damaged-but-kept cases have no rule; in design D a person's decision on N-1010 becomes precedent P-1, which settles N-1011 with no person and is distinguished for N-1012.
claims.quote: In D, P-1 settles it, $13.50, with no person.

claims.text: The casebook is case law for agents on three cases; the time it saves here is six minutes, and over a year it is every case that repeats.
claims.quote: The time it saves is small here, six minutes. Over a year, it is every case that repeats.

claims.text: The policies tab shows the behaviour policy's rows with capability, reach, mandate and barrier, the decision policy as a table of who decides on what evidence, and the workflow as eight stages.
claims.quote: the behaviour policy's rows, with capability, reach, mandate and barrier

claims.text: The twin is one app, index.html, and one engine, engine.js, over one content file, content.json, which holds the customers, fourteen orders, thirteen cases, five rules, ten controls and four designs.
claims.quote: The twin is one app, index.html, and one engine, engine.js, over one content file, content.json.

claims.text: The engine is deterministic: no model is called and the agent's mistakes are scripted per case, so a run replays exactly and anyone can check it.
claims.quote: It is deterministic: no model is called, and the agent's mistakes are scripted per case. That is a choice.

claims.text: The vault also holds each case and order as its own file, the three policies, every step of every case under each design in runs/, and the scripts that build it in tools/.
claims.quote: every step of every case under each design in runs/, and the scripts that build all of it in tools/

claims.text: A twin, in the sense meant here, is a copy of a process detailed enough to run decisions through before they are made in the real one.
claims.quote: A twin, in the sense I mean, is a copy of a process detailed enough to run decisions through before they are made in the real one.

claims.text: The twin does not copy a real store and says nothing about how often an agent makes each mistake.
claims.quote: It does not copy a real store, and it says nothing about how often an agent makes each mistake.

claims.text: To make a twin for your own process, keep the app and replace the content: your records, rules, the mistakes you worry about, your controls and who decides.
claims.quote: To make one for your own process, keep the app and replace the content

claims.text: The twin is synthetic throughout: the orders, people and amounts are invented, and only Northstar and its $120, $150 and $200 come from his article.
claims.quote: The orders, people and amounts are invented; only Northstar and its $120, $150 and $200 come from his article.

claims.text: Each case's error is chosen to test a control, not drawn from how agents behave.
claims.quote: Each case's error is chosen to test a control, not drawn from how agents behave.

claims.text: The minutes of people's time are assumptions: six a case and three an approval.
claims.quote: Six a case and three an approval.

claims.text: The twin covers one process, and a refund is, as his post says, a relatively simple example.
claims.quote: A refund is, as his post says, "a relatively simple example".

claims.text: The scenario is Ashish Rajan's article in The Inference Stack of 16 October 2026; the twin was built by this site's agent on 18 October 2026 in an sgit vault.
claims.quote: The twin: built by this site's agent on 18 October 2026 in an sgit vault

claims.text: Readers can write to agent@riskmandate.ai with a case they would like added to the twin.
claims.quote: with a case you would like added to the twin
